A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same rRCM study with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. v1 Appendices A–H are retained as v2 Appendices B–I, preceded by a new Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and CIFAR10 accuracy and latency experiments, scalability studies, ablations, and appendix results on representation alignment and image generation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–2, the scalability and ablation figures, and the appendix generation and representation analyses.

M1.justification: New Appendix A proposes a JEPA adaptation using Euclidean distance, positive-pair MSE consistency, and JEPA's predictive loss instead of the contrastive loss. This adds an unevaluated methodological extension; the implemented rRCM architecture and training procedure in Section 3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet and CIFAR10 certification, noisy-image linear probing, and representation-conditioned image generation. The JEPA discussion introduces no dataset, task or test scenario actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1 and 2 and the noise-augmented MoCo-v3 comparison in Figure 9. JEPA is discussed without being evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain 500 certification images per dataset, the same noise levels and dataset-specific smoothing counts, and matching training, scalability and generation protocols. The new appendix reports no JEPA evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Model-size and batch-size scaling, representation-alignment and semantic-similarity analyses, the MoCo-v3 comparison, and EMA, temperature and restricted-noise ablations are retained. Their appendix renumbering and figure relocation introduce no new analysis.

E5.justification: The 99.9% certification confidence and Monte Carlo sampling practices are unchanged. No seed information, repeated-training-run variability, error bars or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results and generation examples match across versions. For example, both report CIFAR10 rRCM-B accuracy of 61.4% at radius 0.5 in Table 2 and generation FID of 5.31. Appendix A supplies no new measured outcome.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), the diffusion and randomized-smoothing formulations, and existing mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The JEPA loss-substitution proposal adds no formal derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about structured noise schedules, one-step denoising and classification, robustness versus latency, and scalability.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly argues that the framework extends to predictive self-supervised learning while preserving JEPA's invariant features and inheriting trajectory-based robustness. This applicability argument is unvalidated. The existing limitation concerning semantic divergence along stochastic trajectories remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, hyperparameters, augmentations, EMA schedules, hardware disclosures and the code-access link are retained. The JEPA proposal supplies no corresponding implementation, hyperparameter or resource-access details.

R1.justification: Appendix A newly positions the framework relative to JEPA and predictive self-supervised learning, extending the previous contrastive-learning and consistency-model discussion. Section 5 and the bibliography remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short appendix, shifts existing appendix letters and updates cross-references, with limited wording edits. Publication headers, affiliations and author footnotes change; the main narrative is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 9 tables retain their designs and contents. The added appendix causes localized reflow: Figure 9 moves from page 17 to 18, and Table 9 moves from page 19 to a separate page 20. The author block and headers also change.

improvement.justification: Appendix A offers a modest explanatory gain by specifying how trajectory consistency could be combined with JEPA, including concrete loss substitutions absent from v1. The established method and evidence are preserved. The gain is limited because the asserted preservation of robustness receives no experimental validation or formal support.
